printed_headline_estimate: One-way chi-square goodness-of-fit test across 5 water source categories (streams = 36, wells = 24, boreholes = 18, taps = 8, springs = 14 vs. uniform expected frequency = 20 each): chi-square = 22.8, df = 4, critical value = 9.488, p = 0.0001388, n = 100 (PDF pp. 6, 9 Table 1, 12-13).
publication_year_note: Published in The Journal of Engineering Geology, Vol. 36, No. 1, March 2026, pp. 15-30 (Received: 30 December, 2025; Revised: 31 January, 2026; Accepted: 3 February, 2026; copyright 2026).
rationale: The full text reports only one inferential statistical test: a univariate one-way chi-square goodness-of-fit test (chi-square = 22.8, df = 4, p = 0.0001388, n = 100) evaluating whether household reliance across five water source categories (36 streams, 24 wells, 18 boreholes, 8 taps, and 14 springs) departs from a uniform distribution of 20 per category. Although the paper discusses Camwater tariffs and connection fees, weak decree implementation, institutional gaps, and minimal community engagement, all policy, governance, tariff, and participation material is purely descriptive or qualitative narrative, with no inferential test linking any legal/institutional/tariff/participation exposure (Criterion 2) to a water or sanitation access contrast.
